msi_eq_hard.why: injection under an explicit EQ policy and a hard deadline
msi_eq_hard.notes: The IBM snapshot has no S duration; sx (same cost) stands in for the S correction.

msi_hard_1000.why: same, with a 1000 ns hard deadline (above the 600 ns vendor claim)
msi_hard_1000.notes: The IBM snapshot has no S duration; sx (same cost) stands in for the S correction.

msi_hard_3000.why: injection with a conditional S-like fix-up inside a hard 3000 ns reaction deadline
msi_hard_3000.notes: The IBM snapshot has no S duration; sx (same cost) stands in for the S correction.

msi_hard_tight.why: same, with a 200 ns hard deadline (below the 600 ns vendor claim)
msi_hard_tight.notes: Intended UNSAFE on IBM (hi = 600 ns > 200 ns). The IBM snapshot has no S duration; sx (same cost) stands in for the S correction.

msi_soft_within.why: same fix-up with a soft (non-hard) deadline of 3000 ns
msi_soft_within.notes: Non-hard within. The IBM snapshot has no S duration; sx (same cost) stands in for the S correction.

msi_two_stage.why: two-stage injection: S fix-up then a Z fix-up from a second result, both under hard deadlines
msi_two_stage.notes: The IBM snapshot has no S duration; sx (same cost) stands in for the S correction.
